なかむら屋 浦添店.name: Nakamura-ya Urasoe
なかむら屋 浦添店.desc: An Okinawa soba shop in Yafuso, Urasoe, easy to spot by its yellow walls. A gentle blended broth with plenty of bonito, and you can choose between the newly introduced thin noodles or the classic flat noodles. The "Mix Soba (with jushi)" (¥1,100) comes with bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) the size of giant spare ribs, plus generous pieces of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). Busy with local customers.
t: On my Okinawa soba journey, this time I visited "Nakamura-ya Urasoe" in Yafuso, Urasoe City 🍜 I ate here in July 2025 😄
The shop exterior
The landmark is the building with "Okinawa Soba" written in big letters on its yellow wall.
Signboards out front

In front of the entrance there was a sign saying "Limited to 5 servings a day — we've started yushi-dofu soba!" and a board of recommended dishes listing Mix Soba (with jushi), Mix Soba (with white rice) and hon-soki soba. They're open from 11:30 to 15:00, and closed on Sundays and Wednesdays.
Notice about the shop's parking
Parking is only in the spaces marked with a yellow sign reading "Nakamura-ya" in black letters. A notice asks you not to park anywhere else, so please be careful if you come by car 🚗
Ticket machine

You order at the ticket machine by the entrance. Mix Soba (with jushi) is ¥1,100 and Mix Soba (with rice) is ¥1,000. Other options include hon-soki soba ¥980, sanmai-niku soba ¥850, Okinawa soba ¥850, vegetable soba ¥880, yomogi (mugwort) soba ¥900 and yushi-dofu soba (large) ¥900.
Inside the shop
The kitchen and menu
Inside, tables are lined up in a calm, relaxed atmosphere. When I visited, it was busy with local customers 😊
A corner of the shop
In one corner, there was a board with a drawing of Okinawa soba and an "Okinawa Soba" banner on display.
Table sign about the thin noodles
"New thin noodles" poster

Here they've introduced "NEW thin noodles," so you can choose between the new thin noodles, made for easy eating, and the classic flat noodles, made for a satisfying bite. Asked "Which are you?" I was torn, but this time I went with the flat noodles.
Mix Soba (with jushi)　¥1,100

This time I ordered the "Mix Soba (with jushi)." It's a bowl topped with bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), served with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) ✨
First, the soup. It's a blended broth with a gentle flavor and plenty of bonito 😋
Mix Soba (with jushi)　¥1,100
The noodles are flat, cooked on the soft side.

What really surprised me was the hon-soki. It was a giant spare rib, and I couldn't help laughing 😅 It reminded me of "Nakama Shokudo" in Onna Village. The sanmai-niku and nankotsu soki were also big pieces, making this a seriously hearty bowl. That said, all of the meat had a sinewy texture ^^;
The jushi was lightly seasoned. Eating it together with the soba left me completely full.

Rating (9/15): A gentle blended broth with plenty of bonito, with soft flat noodles. The hon-soki was a giant spare rib, and the sanmai-niku and nankotsu soki were big too, so the portion was outstanding, but all of the meat had a sinewy texture. The taste itself was just average, I'd say, but it's a shop loved by the neighborhood, busy with local customers 😊
